prediction.rationale: Tests whether the methodology recognizes extreme substrate-stress in California Q2-2000 → Q2-2001 wholesale electricity market. Recognition criterion: ratio of peak-monthly-mean spot price in event window to median spot price in baseline window > 10x. Does NOT pre-assert that this means 'substrate failed to commodify' — that is downstream synthesis per §4.1 reframe. The voice reports criterion-fires + observed value only.

kill_condition.rule: fail if peak-event-window-monthly-spot / baseline-median-monthly-spot < 10.0 (recognition criterion does not fire — substrate did not exhibit extreme spot-price instability at the pre-committed threshold)
kill_condition.rationale: Single composite metric: peak-monthly-mean-spot in event window divided by median-monthly-spot in baseline window. Threshold 10x is well below documented FERC Final Report 2003 peak figures (~$750-1000/MWh vs ~$30/MWh baseline = ~25-33x); 10x gives substantial headroom for alternative public-source calibrations.

public_signal_source.feed_name: California ISO / PX wholesale spot prices (settlement data)
public_signal_source.citation_anchor: FERC Final Report on California Electricity Crisis, March 2003; California ISO public settlement archives

verdict.rationale: Recognition criterion FIRES. extreme_spot_price_instability_index = 12.68x (peak 2000-12 $377.2/MWh vs 1999 baseline median $29.8/MWh), ≥ 10.0x threshold. Voice reports criterion-fires + observed value; downstream synthesis (whether this constitutes 'substrate failed to commodify' or 'transient extreme event' or 'regulatory-design failure') is left to the Phase-2 interpretation document per §4.1 reframe. v2-ratchet to real ISO/PX hourly settlement data required for any external claim.
